name: Hakha Chin (Hakha Lai)

ancestors.notes: Hakha Chin (Lai) is a Central Kuki-Chin (Kuki-Chin proper) language descended from Proto-Kuki-Chin (VanBik 2009).

notes: Hakha Chin (Lai, Baibum), spoken in Chin State, Myanmar and diaspora (Indianapolis, Ottawa). Central Kuki-Chin branch, Sino-Tibetan. Latin-based 'Hakha alphabet' orthography; a Mon-Burmese-based alternative script also exists but Latin is primary (Wikipedia; Peterson 2003). Doubled vowel letters ⟨aa ee ii uu oo⟩ mark phonemic vowel length -- earn their keys because the doubled letter is the orthography's own device for a single long-vowel phoneme, not two short vowels in sequence (AGENTS.md test 2). ⟨o⟩ alone maps to /ɔ/ per the five-vowel inventory reported (i e a ɔ u); ⟨ph th kh ch chh⟩ spell the aspirated stop/affricate series; ⟨ng⟩ the velar nasal. Pre-aspirated ⟨hm hn hng hl hr⟩ spell voiceless sonorants, mirroring the same Kuki-Chin pattern documented for Mizo (Chhangte 1993) and cited for Hakha by Peterson (2003) and Baclawski (2012). Final consonants are restricted to /p t k m n ŋ l r j w/ and may carry glottalisation or one of rising/falling/low lexical tone (Peterson 2003) which is not orthographically marked in ordinary text, so tone is left unrepresented here rather than fabricated. Diphthong digraphs (ia iu ui ua ei eu oi ai au) each spell one syllable nucleus (AGENTS.md test 2), not a vowel sequence across a syllable boundary.
